chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
Affliction, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singles out the believer for, was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام,

so he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked, “Who among the people is most severely afflicted in the world?” He said, “The Prophets, then those most like them, then those most like them.” Then the believer is afflicted according to the measure of his faith and the excellence of his deeds. So whoever has sound faith and good deeds, his affliction becomes more intense; and whoever has feeble faith and weak deeds, his affliction is less.

key_terms.أَعْمَالِهِ: his deeds, especially their goodness and excellence
key_terms.إِيمَانِهِ: his faith, by whose measure the believer is tested
key_terms.النَّبِيُّونَ: the Prophets عليهم السلام, described here as the most severely tested
key_terms.الْبَلَاءُ: affliction, trial, or testing sent upon a person

ai.seo_question: Why do the Prophets and stronger believers face the most severe afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the severest worldly afflictions fall first upon the Prophets عليهم السلام, then upon those most similar to them in rank and virtue. It explains that a believer’s trials correspond to the strength of his iman and the goodness of his deeds, so greater spiritual worth is often accompanied by greater testing.
